newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria depo rates rise on tax, reserves payments.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria depo rates rise on tax, reserves payments.

text.p: Bulgaria's interbank deposit rates rose on Friday due to higher demand for funds for payment of commercial banks' minimum required reserves and taxes, dealers said.

"Demand for levs was very high as the deadline expires today for banks to pay their reserves for July with the central bank and for corporate tax advance payment for August," a commercial bank dealer said.
Bulgaria's commercial banks are required to hold 11 percent of their deposits as minimum reserves with the central bank.
Depo rates for overnight or two-day deposits were 1.2-1.3 percent annually against 1.2 percent on Thursday.
One-week deposits traded at 1.8-2.0 percent annually against 1.6 percent and two-week deposits at 2.7 percent against 2.5 percent.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 2.62 percent on Thursday, higher than 1.53 percent on Wednesday, a central bank official said.
The central bank said on Thursday it will raise its main interest rate to 5.70 percent, effective Monday. The main rate is now set at 5.59 percent annually.
